items.title: Neuromodulation of Motivation and Reward Oscillations
items.summary: Cannabis use disorder (CUD) and major depressive disorder (MDD) are among the most prevalent psychiatric conditions in the United States, affecting an estimated 20.6 million and 21 million adults respectively. Both disorders are characterized by anhedonia, diminished motivation, and blunted neural reward sensitivity. This shared dysregulated reward-processing may reflect a common prefrontal oscillatory dysfunction, centralized in mesolimbic dopaminergic reward pathways. items.title: Trial of Self-Applied Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy
items.summary: This purpose of this study is to evaluate whether transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) improves chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) symptoms by assessing changes in daily symptom trajectories following treatment initiation. The study will also examine potential mechanisms of action through longitudinal assessment of inflammatory biomarkers, corticospinal excitability, and autonomic nervous system function.

items.summary: Background: People with substance use disorder (SUD) often have changes in brain function that can make it difficult to control drug-seeking behavior. These changes may heighten the urge to use drugs or lessen the desire to seek nondrug-related rewards. Researchers want to know how a technique called transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) may cause changes in brain activity that may help people with SUD. items.summary: Background: \- Functional and structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques have allowed researchers to map and study how the brain works when at rest and when engaged in specific tasks. items.title: Temporal Interference Stimulation Combined With Tai Chi for Mild Cognitive Impairment
items.summary: This study aims to evaluate whether individualized hippocampal transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) combined with Tai Chi training can improve cognitive function and dual-task performance in individuals with mild cognitive impairment. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either active or sham individualized tTIS combined with Tai Chi training for 8 weeks. The study will also investigate changes in brain structure and function using neuroimaging and assess whether the intervention effects are maintained during follow-up.

items.summary: In the modern society, sleep loss has become a global concern. items.title: Walking delays auditory processing in humans alongside a global shift in aperiodic neural activity
items.summary: Natural sensory processing unfolds during movement, yet human electrophysiology is usually measured under enforced stillness. items.title: Just-in-Time Neuromodulation: A Precision, State-Dependent Paradigm for On-Demand Brain Intervention
items.summary: Neuromodulation is commonly delivered on fixed schedules, whereas psychiatric and neurological symptoms fluctuate over time. Just-in-Time Neuromodulation (JiT-NM) offers a framework for aligning intervention with the emergence or escalation of clinically relevant neural or symptomatic states. We propose three essential components: targeting the desired state, a state-detection system, and a neuromodulatory intervention capable of acting within a clinically useful time window. items.title: Individualized AI-driven Neuromodulation Selectively Enhances and Reorganizes Human Tongue Sensorimotor Networks.
items.summary: Precise modulation of brain networks for tongue motor and sensory control (TMSC) is critical for neruorehabilitation. Existing neuromodulation approaches use fixed targets, ignoring individual network architecture. We present an AI-driven, individualized fMRI neuromodulation (iNM) platform adaptively targeting subject-specific TMSC networks in real-time. Using a neurofunctional twin built from each participant's anatomy and function, iNM reinforces targeted activity and suppresses competing states. items.title: Single-probe, high-yield spatial mapping of diverse short RNA motifs
items.summary: Spatial transcriptomics has revolutionized our understanding of RNA biology. Hybridization-based methods map mRNA transcripts by tiling multiple labeled probes along each molecule to generate a visible fluorescent signal, restricting applicability to long transcripts. Short RNA motifs, consequently, can only accommodate a single probe and remain a spatially invisible dimension of RNA biology. Here we present SMOOTHY-FISH, a single probe strategy that directly visualizes short RNA motifs at the single-molecule resolution. items.title: Thalamic stereo-EEG detects sleep stages N2 and N3 with discrimination approaching scalp EEG
items.summary: Sleep and epilepsy interact strongly during sleep stages N2 and N3, when synchronization of brain rhythms is increased. Sleep staging relies on scalp EEG, which is often absent or incomplete during stereo-EEG monitoring and unavailable from implanted devices, while thalamic leads are increasingly implanted for epilepsy neuromodulation. items.summary: A scientific team supported in part by NIH has developed a new, ultra-high-resolution brain imaging system that can reconstruct microscopic brain structures that are disrupted in neurological and neuropsychiatric brain disorders. items.title: High-tech sticker can identify real human emotions
items.summary: Saying one thing while feeling another is part of being human, but bottling up emotions can have serious psychological consequences like anxiety or panic attacks. To help health care providers tell the difference, a team led by scientists at Penn State has created a stretchable, rechargeable sticker that can detect real emotions — by measuring things like skin temperature and heart rate — even when users put on a brave face.  The researchers recently unveiled the wearable patch that can simultaneously and accurately track multiple emotional signals in a study published in the journal Nano Letters.
